steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper proposing a Mamba-based model for stock price prediction. Motivate stock prediction, go over traditional time series and neural sequence models (LSTM, attention, Transformer) and how they've been used for stocks, introduce Mamba, and present our model.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Why predict stock prices
- Limits of ARIMA; AI and sequence modeling
- RNN/LSTM, attention, attention-based CNN-LSTM
- Transformer and BERT
- Prior models applied to stock prediction
- The Mamba model
- Our proposal: MambaStock

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Motivation
  - stock market important in economic development
  - high return -> attention from institutions and investors
  - complex volatility -> sometimes huge loss
  - predicting price changes helps investors avoid risk
- ARIMA and AI
  - ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model): cannot describe nonlinear series, many preconditions, no remarkable results in stock forecasting
  - rapid development of AI -> more researchers apply AI to financial market
  - sequence modeling (natural language, protein, stock price sequences) important in AI research (cite)
  - neural networks most representative, strong nonlinear generalization ability
- LSTM / attention
  - RNN for sequential data; LSTM most commonly used RNN
  - LSTM gate mechanism ~ human memory: remember useful, forget useless (cite)
  - attention mechanism (cite) ~ human attention
  - ACNN widely used for sequence modeling (cite) and complex dependency capturing (cite)
  - ACNN + LSTM: self-attention based seq2seq (cite) model to encode/decode sequential data
  - solves long-term dependency problem in LSTM; LSTM: long-distance correspondence fitting its structure; ACNN: local and global -> more flexible, robust
- Transformer
  - most successful sequential self-attention model (cite); better long sequences in NLP experiments
  - BERT with pretraining better than basic Transformer (cite); pretraining improves performance
- Applied to stocks
  - Box and Jenkins: ARIMA for time-series forecasting (cite)
  - ARIMA-NN: hybrid ARIMA + neural network (cite)
  - Shi et al.: attention-based CNN-LSTM + XGBoost hybrid (cite)
  - neural network-enhanced state space Kalman Filter models recently
  - TL-KF: Kalman Filter + LSTM + Transformer for stock prediction (cite)
- Mamba
  - significant advancement in sequence modeling (cite)
  - S4 + selection mechanism + scan module = S6
  - captures nonlinear patterns; linear-time complexity -> large-scale datasets
  - selection mechanism adapts dynamically to patterns/structures; scan module scans state spaces for relevant info
- MambaStock
  - Mamba popular for sequence tasks, but financial time series unexplored
  - MambaStock: mines historical stock data, no meticulous feature engineering or extensive preprocessing
  - empirical studies across various stocks: better than traditional methods; helps investors and institutions
  - code at https://github.com/zshicode/MambaStock; data from Tushare (www.tushare.pro), publicly available

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The stock market plays an important role in economic development. Because stocks have high returns, more and more institutions and investors are paying attention to the stock market. But the stock market has complex volatility, and sometimes this brings huge losses to institutions or investors. Because of this risk, research on and prediction of the change of the stock price can help investors avoid the risk.

The traditional time series model ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model) can not describe nonlinear time series, it needs many preconditions to be satisfied before modeling, and it does not achieve remarkable results in stock forecasting. In recent years artificial intelligence theory and technology developed rapidly, and more and more researchers apply artificial intelligence methods to the financial market. Also, the sequence modeling problem is important in artificial intelligence research, for natural language sequences, protein sequences, stock price sequences and so on. Neural networks are the most representative artificial intelligence method, and they have strong nonlinear generalization ability.

Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) was adopted to analyze sequential data with a neural network architecture, and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is the most commonly used RNN. LSTM introduced a gate mechanism in RNN. This can be seen as a simulation of human memory, because humans remember useful information and forget useless information. The Attention Mechanism can be seen as a simulation of human attention, because humans pay attention to useful information and ignore useless information. Attention-based Convolutional Neural Networks (ACNN) are widely used for sequence modeling and for capturing complex dependencies. When ACNN and LSTM are combined, we get a self-attention based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) model that encodes and decodes sequential data. This model can solve the long-term dependency problem in LSTM, so it can model long sequences better. LSTM can capture particular long-distance correspondence that fits the structure of LSTM itself, and ACNN can capture both local and global correspondence. So this architecture is more flexible and robust.

- Transformer
  - most successful sequential self-attention model; better long sequences in NLP experiments
  - BERT with pretraining better than basic Transformer
- Applied to stocks
  - Box and Jenkins: ARIMA; ARIMA-NN hybrid; Shi et al. attention-based CNN-LSTM + XGBoost
  - neural network-enhanced state space Kalman Filter models; TL-KF (Kalman Filter + LSTM + Transformer)
- Mamba
  - S4 + selection mechanism + scan module = S6; nonlinear patterns; linear-time complexity
  - selection mechanism adapts; scan module finds relevant info in state spaces
- MambaStock
  - Mamba unexplored for financial time series; MambaStock, no feature engineering or extensive preprocessing
  - better than traditional methods across various stocks
  - code: https://github.com/zshicode/MambaStock; data: Tushare (www.tushare.pro), public

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The stock market plays an important role in economic development. Because stocks have high returns, more and more institutions and investors are paying attention to the stock market. But the stock market has complex volatility, and sometimes this brings huge losses to institutions or investors. Because of this risk, research on and prediction of the change of the stock price can help investors avoid the risk.

The traditional time series model ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model) can not describe nonlinear time series, it needs many preconditions to be satisfied before modeling, and it does not achieve remarkable results in stock forecasting. In recent years artificial intelligence theory and technology developed rapidly, and more and more researchers apply artificial intelligence methods to the financial market. Also, the sequence modeling problem is important in artificial intelligence research, for natural language sequences, protein sequences, stock price sequences and so on. Neural networks are the most representative artificial intelligence method, and they have strong nonlinear generalization ability.

Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) was adopted to analyze sequential data with a neural network architecture, and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is the most commonly used RNN. LSTM introduced a gate mechanism in RNN. This can be seen as a simulation of human memory, because humans remember useful information and forget useless information. The Attention Mechanism can be seen as a simulation of human attention, because humans pay attention to useful information and ignore useless information. Attention-based Convolutional Neural Networks (ACNN) are widely used for sequence modeling and for capturing complex dependencies. When ACNN and LSTM are combined, we get a self-attention based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) model that encodes and decodes sequential data. This model can solve the long-term dependency problem in LSTM, so it can model long sequences better. LSTM can capture particular long-distance correspondence that fits the structure of LSTM itself, and ACNN can capture both local and global correspondence. So this architecture is more flexible and robust.

The Transformer is the most successful self-attention based model for sequential learning. Experiments in natural language processing show that the Transformer can model long sequences better. Bidirectional Encoder Representation Transformer (BERT) with pretraining can perform better than the basic Transformer. Pretraining is a way to significantly improve the performance of the Transformer (BERT).

These models have been applied for stock prediction. Box and Jenkins used ARIMA for time-series forecasting. ARIMA-NN improved time-series forecasting with a hybrid model of ARIMA and a neural network. Shi et al. proposed a hybrid model of attention-based CNN-LSTM and XGBoost for stock prediction. Recently, state space Kalman Filter models enhanced with neural networks have been applied for time-series forecasting. TL-KF proposed the Kalman Filter together with LSTM and Transformer for stock prediction.

The Mamba model is a significant advancement in sequence modeling. It outperforms the traditional approach by using a structured state space sequence model (S4) with a selection mechanism and a scan module, which is called S6. Mamba is very good at capturing nonlinear patterns in sequential data, which has been a challenge for traditional time series models. Its main strength is that it models sequences efficiently with linear-time complexity, so it is suitable for processing large-scale datasets. The selection mechanism lets it adapt dynamically to different patterns and structures in the data, which makes predictions more accurate. Also, the scan module scans through the state spaces to identify relevant information for making predictions.

Because it is versatile and adaptable, Mamba has been a popular choice for various sequence modeling tasks. But the application of Mamba to financial time series has not been explored yet. So this paper proposes a Mamba-based model to predict the stock price, named MambaStock. MambaStock is a novel approach to stock price prediction. It mines historical stock market data effectively to forecast future prices accurately, and it does not need meticulous feature engineering or extensive preprocessing. Empirical studies across various stocks show that MambaStock is better than traditional methods, and it gives precise predictions that can significantly inform investment decisions. This precision is very valuable for investors and institutions who want to maximize returns while minimizing risks, and it shows the large potential of Mamba in time-series forecasting. The source code of this paper is available at https://github.com/zshicode/MambaStock. The data is downloaded from Tushare (www.tushare.pro), and the stock price data on Tushare is publicly available.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Stock market plays an important role in economic development. Due to the high returns of stocks, the stock market has attracted more and more attention from institutions and investors. However, due to the complex volatility of the stock market, it sometimes brings huge losses to institutions or investors. Considering this risk, research on and prediction of the change of the stock price can help investors avoid the risk.

The traditional time series model ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model) can not describe nonlinear time series, needs to satisfy many preconditions before modeling, and can not achieve remarkable results in stock forecasting. In recent years, with the rapid development of artificial intelligence theory and technology, more and more researchers apply artificial intelligence methods to the financial market. On the other hand, the sequence modeling problem, focusing on natural language sequences, protein sequences, stock price sequences, and so on, is important in artificial intelligence research [1,2]. The most representative artificial intelligence method is neural networks, which have strong nonlinear generalization ability.

Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) was adopted for analyzing sequential data via a neural network architecture, and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is the most commonly used RNN. LSTM introduced a gate mechanism in RNN, which can be seen as a simulation of human memory: humans remember useful information and forget useless information [3,4]. The Attention Mechanism [5] can be seen as a simulation of human attention: humans pay attention to useful information and ignore useless information. Attention-based Convolutional Neural Networks (ACNN) are widely used for sequence modeling [6,7] and complex dependency capturing [8,9]. Combining ACNN and Long Short-Term Memory gives a self-attention based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) [10] model to encode and decode sequential data. This model can solve the long-term dependency problem in LSTM, and hence it can better model long sequences. LSTM can capture particular long-distance correspondence that fits the structure of LSTM itself, while ACNN can capture both local and global correspondence. Therefore, this architecture is more flexible and robust.

Transformer [5] is the most successful self-attention based model for sequential learning. Experiments on natural language processing demonstrate that Transformer can better model long sequences. Bidirectional Encoder Representation Transformer (BERT) with pretraining [11] can perform better than the basic Transformer, and pretraining is a method to significantly improve the performance of Transformer (BERT).

The models mentioned above have been applied for stock prediction. Box and Jenkins [12] adopted ARIMA for time-series forecasting. ARIMA-NN [13] improved time-series forecasting using a hybrid ARIMA and neural network model. Shi et al. [14] proposed an attention-based CNN-LSTM and XGBoost hybrid model for stock prediction. Recently, neural network-enhanced state space Kalman Filter models have been applied for time-series forecasting. TL-KF [15] proposed the Kalman Filter along with LSTM and Transformer for stock prediction [14].

The Mamba model [16] represents a significant advancement in sequence modeling. This model outperforms the traditional approach by incorporating a structured state space sequence model (S4) with a selection mechanism and a scan module, known as S6. Mamba excels at capturing nonlinear patterns in sequential data, which has historically been a challenge for traditional time series models. Its core strength lies in its ability to efficiently model sequences with linear-time complexity, making it suitable for processing large-scale datasets. The selection mechanism allows it to dynamically adapt to different patterns and structures within the data, enabling more accurate predictions. Additionally, the scan module scans through the state spaces to identify relevant information for making predictions.

Due to its versatility and adaptability, Mamba has been a popular choice for various sequence modeling tasks. However, the application of Mamba to financial time series remains to be explored. Therefore, this paper proposes a Mamba-based model to predict the stock price, named MambaStock. The MambaStock model, a novel approach to stock price prediction, effectively mines historical stock market data to accurately forecast future prices, without the need for meticulous feature engineering or extensive preprocessing. Empirical studies across various stocks demonstrate the superiority of MambaStock over traditional methods, delivering precise predictions that can significantly inform investment decisions. This precision is invaluable to investors and institutions seeking to maximize returns while minimizing risks, and highlights the great potential of Mamba in time-series forecasting. The source code of this paper is available at https://github.com/zshicode/MambaStock. The data is downloaded from Tushare (www.tushare.pro), and the stock price data on Tushare is publicly available.
